d: The tight junctions between neighboring Sertoli cells. They seal off the inner compartment of the tubule and hide meiotic germ cells, whose antigens appear only after puberty, from the immune system.
A protein that Sertoli cells secrete under FSH. It binds testosterone and keeps its concentration inside the seminiferous tubule far above the serum level, which spermatogenesis requires.
The network of testicular veins in the spermatic cord that wraps the testicular artery and cools incoming blood by countercurrent exchange. Its dilation is a varicocele.
The final stage of spermatogenesis, with no cell division. A round spermatid builds an acrosome from the Golgi apparatus, condenses its nucleus, grows a flagellum and sheds its extra cytoplasm.
Compression of the small veins under the tunica albuginea when the filled sinusoids press against it. This traps blood in the corpora cavernosa and keeps the erect penis rigid.
A smooth muscle-like cell that wraps the outside of a seminiferous tubule. Its contractions push immotile sperm and fluid toward the rete testis.

The smooth muscle layer of the scrotal skin that wrinkles in the cold to lose less heat. It is continuous with Colles fascia of the perineum and Scarpa fascia of the abdomen, the plane along which Fournier gangrene spreads.
The packet of excess cytoplasm that a spermatid sheds as it becomes a spermatozoon. Sertoli cells engulf and digest it, one of their support jobs inside the tubule.
